fact: The agreed Project Workflow orders Fact Management, Design, Implement, Review, Fact Management, then Handoff.
The first Fact Management stage uses a single model in the Main Session to reconcile and commit the full list of Taskbook Facts before Design.
Fact Management pauses for the user when a supplied fact overlaps a registered fact and the requested update or separate scope is unclear.
Fact Management tags supplied facts with the active taskbook's label so later stages can distinguish them from project background.
Designer and Implementer treat the active taskbook's tagged facts as the primary inputs for its scope and escalate contradictions with applicable project facts.
The Taskbook plugin selects the next Work State and builds the context, prompt, model, and tool set before creating or continuing each Subagent.
At the Design stage the plugin creates three Designer sessions. It creates one Implementer session after the approved design taskbook has been committed.
Agents report structured outcomes to the plugin. The plugin validates the result, records the next transition, and dispatches the next Work Turns.
Each Work Turn is bound to a task, stage, round, Subagent, input version, and attempt. The plugin accepts one matching result after that turn settles.
The plugin permits one in-flight Work Turn per Subagent. It waits for a timed-out turn to settle before retrying that Subagent.
Each Designer drafts a taskbook independently from the same input, then reads both other drafts once all three drafts are submitted.
Each Designer requests changes to Goals or Facts in the other drafts and responds to comments on its own draft. The user resolves persistent disagreements.
Designers use the taskbook's Delivery as an input constraint and propose changes to Goal and Facts.
The plugin commits the final Design taskbook as a Markdown file in .fact and commits its removal at the end of the run.
The plugin retains Designer identities and sessions from Design through Review.
The Lead Designer issues the final Design and Review decisions and decides when to ask the user. A Member Designer sends an escalation to the Lead Designer.
A distinct work prompt has a distinct Work State. An iteration counter can reuse a state when its work prompt remains the same.
The current agent enters Consult with its role's playbook when it has a decision to make, answers questions within its responsibility, and routes other questions to their owner.
A conflict with an authored fact pauses the project workflow for the user's decision.
One Designer member performs the initial Review for a three-person group. The lead coordinates resolution and approval.
The Review participants consider the initial findings and agree on the verdict or the rework request for the candidate.
The plugin supplies the current taskbook Goal, Review prompt, and read-only review tools when dispatching a Designer into Review.
Review covers the Draft Facts produced by the Designer lead, Designer members, and Implementer along with the candidate's behavior and maintainability.
The final Fact Management stage classifies approved Draft Facts, commits them to .fact, and returns the resulting fact diff.
Handoff uses the committed fact diff for pull request reporting and prepares authorized delivery artifacts under its own prompt.
Pi Taskbook owns four named Pi SDK sessions and keeps each seat’s configured model and reasoning level through Design, Implement and Review.
